passage:
Hiroshi: Physio thinks my shin pain is a stress reaction. She wants me off running for six weeks.
Danielle: No way. The marathon is in five weeks and you've trained all year. It has to be something minor.
Hiroshi: She did press on it and I nearly hit the ceiling.
cue: The marathon is in five weeks and you've trained all year. It has to be something minor.
explanation: Danielle decides the injury must be minor because a serious one would wreck Hiroshi's race. The race date has no bearing on what's actually happening in his shin.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_emotion: Danielle isn't just stirring feelings; she infers a medical fact from how bad the alternative would be.

source: Car buyer to a friend · dealership lot
passage: The dealer swears it's never been in an accident, and honestly, it can't have been. We've promised the whole family a lake trip in it on Friday, and I'm not telling the kids it's off. So no, I'm not spending $40 on a history report. Help me pick seat covers?
cue: it can't have been. We've promised the whole family a lake trip in it on Friday
explanation: The buyer decides the SUV is accident-free because the alternative would ruin Friday's lake trip. Whether the car was ever in a crash doesn't depend on the family's plans.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_emotion: It's more than a feeling on display; the buyer treats an unwanted outcome as proof of a fact about the car.

title: Re: FY27 revenue forecast
passage: Thanks for the review, Adaeze. You're right that Q3 bookings came in below plan, and I've trimmed the marketing line to reflect that. But I can't accept a forecast showing a 15% revenue decline next year. A number like that would mean closing the Ashby office and telling the board we've lost a year. Our forecast has to show growth, and I'm confident it's there.
cue: A number like that would mean closing the Ashby office
explanation: Graham accepts the weak Q3 numbers but rejects the decline forecast because of what it would force the company to do. Painful consequences don't make a forecast inaccurate.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_emotion: Graham isn't just stirring feelings; he argues the projection is wrong because acting on it would be painful.

passage: Seeing chatter about the university report saying algae levels in Kestrel Lake are unsafe for swimming. Our town runs on summer visitors. If that report were right, half the shops on Shore Road would be shuttered by August, so no, we're not buying it. Lifeguards are on duty all weekend and the ice cream stand opens at 10!
cue: If that report were right, half the shops on Shore Road would be shuttered by August
explanation: The post rejects the algae findings because accepting them would hurt local businesses. The lake's water quality doesn't depend on what it would mean for the shops.

whyNot.fal_slippery_slope: The post isn't predicting a chain set off by some step; it denies a fact because its implications would be costly.

source: Coach Rory Webb · Wrenford Youth Soccer parent night
passage: Some of you sent me that article saying kids born in the first few months of the year are far more likely to be picked for elite youth teams. I don't believe it. If a kid born in November thinks his birthday decides his future, he'll quit before he starts, and I won't have that. Hard work is what gets players picked, full stop.
cue: If a kid born in November thinks his birthday decides his future, he'll quit before he starts
explanation: Coach Webb rejects the birth-month finding because believing it might discourage younger kids. That's a good reason to talk with players carefully, but it says nothing about whether the pattern is real.

whyNot.fal_slippery_slope: He isn't predicting an unsupported chain from a first step; he denies a factual pattern because believing it could discourage kids.

title: Rare heron sighting at Fen Marsh sparks celebration, and caution
passage: A single photo taken at dusk has Fen Marsh volunteers convinced the great white heron is nesting there for the first time in 30 years. 'If she's back, it means the restoration worked and every muddy Saturday was worth it,' said volunteer chair Silas Pryce. 'So I'm calling it: she's back.' County biologists say the photo is too dark to confirm the species.
cue: If she's back, it means the restoration worked and every muddy Saturday was worth it
explanation: Silas decides the heron is back because that outcome would vindicate years of volunteer work. Wanting it to be true doesn't make a dark photo any clearer; only a confirmed sighting would.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_emotion: Silas's hope is emotional, but his reasoning goes further: he concludes a fact is true because its implications would be so welcome.

passage:
Tomasz: Inspection rated the Mill St bridge deck 'poor', with spalling on two spans.
Renee: Agreed, it's in bad shape. A full closure adds about 15 minutes to east-side ambulance runs. A 10-ton limit keeps ambulances (around 6 tons) moving while banning the gravel trucks that cause most of the wear, so a weight limit is the better call until repairs.
explanation: Renee accepts the inspection's finding, then weighs the consequences of different responses. Using outcomes to choose an action, not to deny a fact, is exactly where consequences belong.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_consequences: Renee doesn't deny the bridge is in poor shape; she uses consequences only to decide what to do about it.

passage: Our shopper survey is in, and it's not what we hoped: 41% say the market is too expensive to visit weekly. We'd love to call that a fluke, but it matches the 18% drop in attendance since spring. Raising stall fees again would push prices even higher, so we're freezing fees for next season and inviting more budget-friendly vendors.
cue: We'd love to call that a fluke, but it matches the 18% drop in attendance
explanation: The market accepts an unwelcome finding because it fits the attendance data, then uses consequences only to choose next steps. Wishes don't override the evidence here.

whyNot.fal_appeal_to_consequences: The market resists wishful thinking about the survey and applies consequences only to the fee decision, where they belong.
